f.pu: The site was established in 1909 to provide legal protection for the millions of seabirds inhabiting the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands at a time in our past when seabirds were being slaughtered by the thousands for their plumage and eggs.
f.re: The site is closed to the public.

f.re: 1. Midway Atoll National Wildlife Refuge and Battle of Midway National Memorial are currently closed to public visitation. 2. Commercial fishing is prohibited and recreational fishing is restricted. 3. Take of coral is prohibited. 4. Discharging or depositing any material or other matter is prohibited.

f.pu: To establish a marine refuge in the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands for the longterm conservation and protection of the unique coral reef ecosystems and the related marine resources and species, to ensure their conservation and natural character.
f.re: It is unlawful for any person: 1. To enter the refuge without a permit. 2. To take for the purpose of sale or sell marine life taken from the refuge. 3. To take marine life in violation of the items in the 'Allowed' section. 4. To set foot on shore, on any emergent land or reef. 5.
